2: A school trip is attended by 16 students, of whom only four know the area. The teacher wants to randomly choose 3 people to go to the shop. Calculate the probability that exactly two of the three chosen people know the area.
3: A block of butter produced by a certain dairy has a nominal mass of 20 dag. During an inspection, 150 randomly chosen blocks of butter were weighed. The results are shown in the table: mass in dag (16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22) with counts (1, 15, 24, 68, 26, 16) respectively. a) Based on the data in the table, calculate the arithmetic mean and the standard deviation of the mass of a block of butter. b) The inspection is considered positive if the average mass equals the nominal mass and the standard deviation does not exceed 1 dag. Did the inspection of the plant turn out positive? Justify your answer.
4: An increasing geometric sequence is given, in which $a_1=12$ and $a_3=27$. a) Determine the ratio of this sequence. b) Write the formula for computing the term $a_n$, for every natural number $n\ge1$. c) Calculate the term $a_6$.
5: Knowing that $0°\le\alpha\le360°$, $\sin\alpha<0$, and $4\tan\alpha=3\sin^2\alpha+3\cos^2\alpha$: a) calculate $\tan\alpha$. b) Mark angle $\alpha$ in the coordinate system and give the coordinates of any point, other than the origin, that lies on the terminal arm of this angle.
7: A sketch shows a district heating channel whose cross-section is a rectangle. Inside the channel there is a pipeline consisting of three pipes, each with an external diameter of 1 m. Calculate the height and width of the heating channel. Round the height to 0.01 m.
9: The roof of a tower has the shape of the lateral surface of a regular quadrilateral pyramid, whose base edge has length 4 m. A lateral face of this pyramid is inclined to the base plane at an angle of $60°$. a) Make an auxiliary drawing and mark the given quantities on it. b) Calculate how many roof tiles must be bought to cover this roof, knowing that 24 tiles are needed to cover $1\,\text{m}^2$. When buying, an extra 8% of tiles should be added as a reserve.
10: The numbers 3 and -1 are roots of the polynomial $W(x)=2x^3+ax^2+bx+30$. a) Determine the values of the coefficients a and b. b) Calculate the third root of this polynomial.
11: The sum $S=\frac{3}{1\cdot4}+\frac{3}{4\cdot7}+\frac{3}{7\cdot10}+\dots+\frac{3}{301\cdot304}+\frac{3}{304\cdot307}$ can be computed as follows: a) write S with each term expressed via the difference of consecutive denominators, b) represent each term of this sum as a difference of fractions, c) compute the sum by cancelling adjacent terms in pairs, except the first and last: $S=1-\frac{1}{307}=\frac{306}{307}$. Proceeding in an analogous way, calculate the sum $S_1=\frac{4}{1\cdot5}+\frac{4}{5\cdot9}+\frac{4}{9\cdot13}+\dots+\frac{4}{281\cdot285}$.
